solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Love helping after fuss

indicators.note: 'after' says the helping comes behind the fuss in the answer

parts.note: fuss means ado, as in 'much ado about nothing'
a helping is a portion or ration of food

explanation.surface: Someone's love expressed by helping out after a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love or worship, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fabulist's revolutionary attitude allowed at first

definitions.note: the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of allowed
revolutionary means turned round, so the word for attitude is read backwards

parts.note: a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A storyteller's rebellious stance was tolerated initially.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek writer of moral animal fables, the archetypal teller of fables.

clue.text: Self-inflicted damage to have purpose

parts.note: to own is to have or possess
a goal is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Harming oneself in order to have some purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: From football, scoring against your own side; figuratively any act that harms oneself.

clue.text: One in Honda car styled like Spider

indicators.note: styled means fashioned or shaped anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A passenger in a Honda car designed like the Alfa Romeo Spider sports model.
explanation.walkthrough: Spider looks like a car name, the capital hiding the arachnid.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resembling a spider or of the class Arachnida.

clue.text: Rude Neo is to the point

parts.note: Neo is the setter, so 'Neo is' becomes I'm
pertinent means relevant, to the point

explanation.surface: The setter, Neo, is being bluntly direct.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves, so Neo is stands for 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means insolent or cheeky, a synonym of discourteous behaviour.

clue.text: Henry going climbing finds drama

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
on means going or happening, as in 'what's on'

explanation.surface: Henry, out mountaineering, comes across a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical Japanese form of masked dance-drama.

clue.text: Historian loses position in province

indicators.note: 'loses' says the letters for position are dropped from the historian's name

parts.note: Thomas Babington Macaulay was a Victorian historian
lay means position or arrangement, as in 'the lay of the land'

explanation.surface: A historian stripped of his post in some province.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay was the 19th-century author of a History of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Portuguese territory on the Chinese coast, now a special administrative region, loosely a province of China.

clue.text: Picture motorway over Russian river?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the motorway letter above the river

parts.note: M is used for motorway in British road names like the M1
the Ural flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A picture of a motorway crossing a Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A large painting done directly on a wall, a type of picture.

clue.text: Letter to Greeks opposed to an Italian import?

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A letter to the Greeks objecting to some Italian product.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as one example of an import.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan red wine, a typical product imported from Italy.

clue.text: Sun forced European supporting former PM to pull out

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath the former PM
forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters of sun are rearranged

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A newspaper pressured a European backer of an ex-premier to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, making 'forced' read as newspaper pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a sword or knife from its scabbard is to pull it out.

clue.text: New wallop's drink brought round — it's for Browning

indicators.note: the drink is wrapped around the other pieces, so 'brought round' signals containment

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to lam is to wallop or thrash; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: Fresh ale is served, apparently in honour of the poet Robert Browning.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet but means tanning, hence the question of what a tanning lamp is for. Wallop is also British slang for beer, a second false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanning lamp emits ultraviolet light to brown the skin, so it is a device for browning.

clue.text: Paris, he messed around, grasping women

indicators.note: messed around says the letters of Paris and he are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Paris, the Trojan prince, philandering with women.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpies were rapacious winged monsters in Greek myth; the word now means greedy, grasping females.

clue.text: Mongrel at the start can't bear hugs

indicators.note: the bear's name wraps around the letter, so 'hugs' signals containment

parts.note: Pooh is the bear created by A. A. Milne

indicators.note: 'at the start' takes just the opening letter of can't

explanation.surface: A mongrel that can't stand being cuddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't bear' reads as one phrase, but 'bear' is a separate piece: Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a dog, especially a mixed-breed mutt.

clue.text: Suggestion about benefit once topped

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the dole is British unemployment benefit

indicators.note: topped means having its top, the first letter, cut off the word once

explanation.surface: A proposal concerning welfare payments that were once scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dole' is the everyday British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolence is a scent or quality that evokes or hints at something, so a suggestion of it.

clue.text: First to detect hidden person in social situation

indicators.note: First to takes just the opening letter of detect

parts.note: inner means hidden or private, as in inner thoughts
party means a person, especially in legal language

explanation.surface: The first to spot a concealed individual in a social setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal evening meal with guests is a kind of social occasion.

clue.text: Everyone in great central room beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the room's name is lopped off

parts.note: a hall is the large main room of a grand house or college

explanation.surface: Everybody in the main hall has lost their head.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun meaning the whole group, every person together, as in 'one for all'.

clue.text: 60s idol first man to get religion

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis
a faith is a religion

explanation.surface: The first man finds religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A British pop singer who was a teen idol of the early 1960s.

clue.text: Cultural expert savaged in Aristotle

indicators.note: savaged means mauled and torn apart, so the letters of in and Aristotle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar of culture is torn to shreds within Aristotle's writings.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies Eastern languages and cultures, so an expert in Asian culture.

clue.text: Might one offer oil trader supply that includes beer?

indicators.note: the jumbled trader wraps around the beer, so it includes it
read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters of trader are bent into a new order

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A merchant's oil supply might include beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but read as 'in a supple way' it is the anagram signal; 'oil' means an oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells paintings could well offer an oil painting for sale.

clue.text: Cutting free stone to be collected by a criminal

indicators.note: the criminal's word gathers up the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: bent is British slang for corrupt or criminal
to rid is to free or clear
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jewel freed from its setting is gathered up by a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' as slang for dishonest, as in 'a bent copper', is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridgement is a shortened version of a text, the result of cutting it down.

clue.text: Some lines about Drugs Enforcement Agency in sport

indicators.note: 'in' places the other pieces within the sport's letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union
on means about or concerning
DEA abbreviates the US drug enforcement agency

explanation.surface: A few lines on drug enforcement in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A short poem with a fixed form and refrain, so a set of verse lines.

clue.text: Wife in A&E shows fear and wonder

indicators.note: 'in' places the wife's letter inside the hospital department's letters

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is taken simply as the letters A and E
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wife in the emergency department is frightened and amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means reverential wonder mixed with dread, exactly fear and wonder combined.

clue.text: Fatty, a pickpocket, got up right away

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the word for got up

parts.note: rose means got up

explanation.surface: A plump pickpocket stood up and immediately left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once' but splits into a letter and its removal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes body fat or fatty tissue.

clue.text: Identify suspect information in digital feature?

parts.note: to finger someone is to identify them as the culprit
a tip is a piece of useful information or a tip-off

explanation.surface: Police identify a suspect from a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' means relating to digits, i.e. fingers, not computers; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers, so the end of one is a feature of a digit, punningly a digital feature.

clue.text: Still time to ride competitively

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even more'

explanation.surface: There is still time to go riding in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse riders compete in eventing, which combines dressage, cross-country and jumping, so this verb means competing on horseback.

clue.text: Dallas family for example embodies success

indicators.note: embodies means takes into its body, so the example letters hold the success

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: A TV family that personifies success.
explanation.walkthrough: Dallas was a long-running US soap about a Texas oil family.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil-rich Texan clan at the centre of the soap opera Dallas, featuring J. R.

clue.text: Good answer by rowdy teen kept in school

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a rowdy 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A sensible reply from an unruly teenager kept behind after school.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: At British schools and colleges, a pupil confined to the premises as punishment has been given this sanction.

clue.text: In charge, English composer, one with cold manner

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An English composer in charge, aloof in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a frosty, unemotional person is called this, after the cold mass of floating ice.

clue.text: Soft wet lump in desert I must leave

indicators.note: must leave says the letter I is removed from the desert's name

parts.note: the Gobi is a desert in Mongolia and China

explanation.surface: A soggy lump in the desert I must abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect and slang word for a lump or clot of slimy matter, such as spit.

clue.text: Exclude posh stars in dull routine

indicators.note: 'in' places the posh letter and the stars inside the dull routine

parts.note: a rut is a boring routine
U means upper-class or posh in British usage
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Keep upper-class celebrities out of tedious routine.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to eliminate a possibility, so to exclude it.

clue.text: Husband gets mum's sister in trouble

parts.note: a mother's sister is an aunt

explanation.surface: A husband lands his wife's aunt in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to plague or disturb persistently, as worries or memories trouble a person.

clue.text: Lover fired on by lunatic

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters of fired, on and by are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lover shot at by a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in a romantic relationship with someone is their partner or sweetheart.
